newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin makes daughter Tatyana official adviser.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin makes daughter Tatyana official adviser.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin appointed his daughter Tatyana Dyachenko as an official adviser on image-making on Monday, the Kremlin said.

Yeltsin's press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing Dyachenko, 37, would be responsible for the president's image. The long-expected appointment formalises the role the president's younger daughter has been playing in the Kremlin since Yeltsin's successful re-election campaign last year.
Yastrzhembsky did not give details of Tatyana's new job. She is a computer mathematician by education and has two sons -- Boris, born in 1981, and Gleb, born in 1995.

Tatyana, the only member of the presidential family with a high political profile, played an important role in the analytical group of Yeltsin's election campaign staff, headed by the liberal reformer Anatoly Chubais.

Chubais has said she should be given the role of "common sense" adviser in the Kremlin. She was instrumental in providing a direct link between the liberals and Yeltsin in the most tense periods of the campaign.
Since then Tatyana has accompanied Yeltsin on most of his trips but hitherto has not been given an official role.
